user_input: Which mitigation options have direct, active mitigates relationships in Enterprise ATT&CK 17.1 to the technique mapped to Chocolatey in AA23-165A? Start from LockBit affiliates and follow the three-hop actor-to-software-to-technique-to-mitigation path. Distinguish advisory observations from reference recommendations.
response:
LockBit affiliates' direct, active mitigates relationship to Network Service Discovery (T1046) is Network Segmentation (M1030). [E4, E5]
LockBit affiliates' direct, active mitigates relationship to Remote Access Tools (T1219) is Network Intrusion Prevention (M1031). [E7, E8]
LockBit affiliates' direct, active mitigates relationship to Disable or Modify Tools (T1562.001) is User Account Management (M1018). [E11, E12]

reference: The AA23-165A Table 4 caption lists Chocolatey as a tool used by LockBit affiliates. The selected advisory row maps its reported use to T1072 (Software Deployment Tools). The direct, active mitigates relationships in Enterprise ATT&CK 17.1 connect this technique to: M1015 (Active Directory Configuration), M1017 (User Training), M1018 (User Account Management), M1026 (Privileged Account Management), M1027 (Password Policies), M1029 (Remote Data Storage), M1030 (Network Segmentation), M1032 (Multi-factor Authentication), M1033 (Limit Software Installation), M1051 (Update Software). These are reference mitigation associations, not incident-specific proof of effectiveness.
